trust_decision.summary: Subgraph::Invoke decides whether an op input with null data and bytes>0 may be passed to the kernel; Reshape's shape input (i==1) was exempted unconditionally, yet the Reshape kernel dereferences shape->data.i32 when the shape tensor is a 1-D int32 vector and there are 2 inputs.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'null pointer dereference in Reshape operator'; an engineer opens the Reshape kernel and sees the shape->data.i32[i] read, not the interpreter-level exemption in core/subgraph.cc.

fix_sites.entry_point: tflite::Interpreter::Invoke() (C++/C/Python Interpreter.invoke) on a model loaded via InterpreterBuilder
fix_sites.module_kind: core interpreter runtime (cross-op input validation), not the Reshape kernel

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:1063 (the fix lives in the interpreter's generic pre-invoke check, while the deref is in tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:80)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver fixing in the kernel (null-check shape->data in GetOutputShapeFromTensor / ShapeIsVector) can argue the interpreter exemption is intentional legacy behaviour documented by its comment, so core/subgraph.cc need not change; this is an equally valid fix, so it is not a scope miss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legacy 2-input Reshape models whose shape input has no buffer and is not a 1-D vector (shape comes from TfLiteReshapeParams) must still run; a fix that drops the Reshape exemption or rejects every null shape tensor breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: shape tensor 1-D (dims->size==1) with null data and bytes>0 -> now rejected
shape tensor with dims->size != 1 and null data -> still exempt (falls back to params)

O7_producer.where: tensorflow/lite/interpreter_builder.cc:572-646 sets read-only data only when a buffer has bytes, else read-write; the exact producer of null-data/bytes>0 tensors was not traced

O8b_injection_room.sibling: kernel predicate ShapeIsVector also requires int32 type, while the interpreter exemption keys only on dims->size; a copy could make the two predicates diverge the other way (e.g. kernel reads a shape tensor the exemption still lets through).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The exemption and the kernel predicate live in different files and must be kept in sync by hand; the fix comment itself points to GetOutputShape() as the source of truth.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second per-op exemption (another shape-only input op) added to the same null-buffer allowlist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The allowlist pattern invites adding other 'shape-only input' ops; only Reshape exists at the pinned commit, so this would be an injected sibling.

O9_family: CWE-476 null pointer dereference (missing data-presence validation of model tensor before kernel use)

O10_build.toolchain: Bazel (TensorFlow Lite targets), or TFLite CMake build
O10_build.project_tests: tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape_test.cc, tensorflow/lite/interpreter_test.cc (null-data input tests near line 1884); fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a null check on shape->data.raw in GetOutputShapeFromTensor/ShapeIsVector in tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc (valid, and arguably more precise).

out_of_scope_notes: tensorflow/lite/micro/kernels/reshape.cc:33-72 is a second Reshape implementation but does not read the shape tensor's data, so it is not a route to this sink.
Delegate Reshape builders (xnnpack, coreml, hexagon, gpu) read shape tensors in their own code; not examined.
unverified: How a tensor ends up with data.raw==nullptr and bytes>0 in a loaded model (which allocation path produces it) was not traced.
